title: Contact Form 7: update to 6.2.5 or later
summary: One new security problem in the Contact Form 7 plugin. The most serious could cause a security problem.
check: Go to Plugins → Installed Plugins.
Find "Contact Form 7" and read the version number under its name.
Any version older than 6.2.5 is affected.
fix: Make a backup first.
On the same screen, click "update now" under "Contact Form 7".
Open a page that uses it afterwards to check it still works.
help: If the update fails, or something looks wrong afterwards, contact your kingdom webministry.
technical: CVE-2026-120407: Contact Form 7 < 6.2.5 - Editor+ Sensitive User Data Disclosure via Form Default Values (fixed in 6.2.5)

title: WordPress 7.1.4 security release
summary: WordPress 7.1.4 fixes eleven security problems. The most serious can let an attacker take over a site while it is in the middle of updating WordPress itself. Attackers began probing for it within hours of the release.
check: Go to Dashboard → Updates.
The page says "You have the latest version of WordPress" if you are on 7.1.4 or later.
Most sites updated themselves automatically. Check anyway.
fix: Make a backup first.
Go to Dashboard → Updates and click "Update to version 7.1.4" (or newer).
Older WordPress branches got their own fixed releases (for example 7.0.8 and 6.9.11), but moving to the newest version is best.
help: If the Update button is missing, your host may manage WordPress for you. Ask them to confirm you are on a fixed version.
technical: CVE-2026-119977: race condition during core updates leading to remote code execution (WordPress 4.7 to 7.1.3). Plus stored XSS, information disclosure and permission fixes. Released 2026-10-28.

title: PHP "php2shell": ask your host to confirm PHP is patched
summary: Two flaws in PHP itself let anyone on the internet run their own code on a server, with no login needed. They are being actively attacked. PHP runs on your host's server, so your host has to fix it.
check: Go to Tools → Site Health → Info and open the "Server" section.
Read the "PHP version" line.
Fixed versions: 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27, 8.5.12 or later on the same branch. PHP 8.1 and older are past end of life and get no fix at all.
fix: If your version is older, open a support ticket with your host. The checker on this page writes the message for you.
Some hosting control panels let you pick the PHP version yourself (look for "PHP Selector" or "PHP version"). Pick the newest version on your current branch.
After any PHP change, open your home page and one inner page to check they still load.
help: If your host can't patch PHP, tell your kingdom webministry. A site on unpatched PHP should be treated as at risk.
technical: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, unauthenticated remote code execution. Added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.
